sources.title: Independent bounded CPU original fence and variants
Natural-log score normalization and featurewise mixture
sources.details: x shape(1,2) times W shape(2,3) gives (1,3) scores [0,0,ln2]. exp gives [1,1,2]; divide by 4 gives [.25,.25,.5]. Sum a_i times [x,2x,3x] over expert axis gives 2.25x=[2.25,4.5]. Zero W gives equal thirds and 2x=[2,4]. Prob axis insertion (1,3,1) broadcasts equally across the two feature coordinates, then sum(1) leaves (1,2).

sources.title: Mixture weights, correctness and output scale
sources.details: The gate equation is a function of x and router weights; it contains no gold answer or correctness frequency. Gate=.5 is therefore a mixing coefficient, not a calibrated expert accuracy. Replacing evaluation targets can change whether the same fixed mixture is correct without changing the gate. Changing an expert's output scale changes weighted output and loss gradients even with unchanged gates; actual small CPU scale variant exhibits that sensitivity. Historical imbalanced-routing possibility is separately supported by original Section 4, not claimed as diagnosed in this example.

sources.title: Continuous mean versus discrete top-2 assignment fraction
sources.details: For T valid positions, P_i=(1/T)sum_t p_ti. For top-k, n_i=sum_t sum_slot 1[chosen_t,slot=i] and assignment share=n_i/(T*k). Here T=39256, k=2, denominator=78512; second layer n=[16209,21137,17745,23421] sums exactly to 78512. Rounded n/78512=[.2065,.2692,.2260,.2983], unlike stored rounded P=[.2875,.1772,.2652,.2701]. Only non-PAD positions are included; layers are counted separately. Stored P is directly checked as the primary aggregate, not reconstructed from unavailable per-token traces.
